target.title: fix(sessions): remap stale same-agent paths into the current state dir
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: persisted absolute `sessionFile` paths for the same agent can survive a state-root move (for example `/home/rai/.openclaw/...` to `/Users/rai/.openclaw/...`) and still be treated as structurally valid.
- Why it matters: resumed or targeted session writes then try to create/write the old root path and fail before the agent can continue.
- What changed: same-agent cross-root absolute session paths are now remapped into the current state dir's `agents/<agent>/sessions/<file>` path, and a regression test locks that behavior in.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): cross-agent fallback behavior and unrelated absolute-path normalization logic were left intact.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #61321
- Related #61321
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause / Regression History (if applicable)

- Root cause: `resolvePathWithinSessionsDir()` preserved structurally valid absolute session paths even when they pointed at the same agent under an old state root.
- Missing detection / guardrail: there was no regression coverage for same-agent cross-root absolute `sessionFile` metadata.
- Prior context (`git blame`, prior PR, issue, or refactor if known): the absolute-path normalization and sibling-agent fallback logic around this area was introduced in February 2026; local blame points at the existing fallback path in `src/config/sessions/paths.ts`.
- Why this regressed now: a machine carrying Linux-rooted persisted session metadata was later used on macOS, so the stale absolute path became invalid only after the root move.
- If unknown, what was ruled out: stale `HOME`, stale `OPENCLAW_HOME`, stale `session.store` override, and provider-specific causes were ruled out locally.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [ ] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/config/sessions.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: a same-agent absolute `sessionFile` from an old root is remapped into the current state dir instead of being preserved.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the failure is in pure path-resolution logic, before session execution or provider behavior.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): nearby cross-root and cross-agent fallback tests cover adjacent logic but not this same-agent remap case.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Resumed or targeted sessions with stale same-agent absolute transcript paths are recovered into the current state dir instead of failing on the old root path.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
old absolute sessionFile (/home/rai/.../agents/shikamaru/sessions/sess-1.jsonl)
  -> treated as structurally valid
  -> write lock tries old root
  -> ENOENT on /home/rai

After:
old absolute sessionFile (/home/rai/.../agents/shikamaru/sessions/sess-1.jsonl)
  -> recognized as same-agent stale root
  -> remapped to current state dir agents/shikamaru/sessions/sess-1.jsonl
  -> write proceeds
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation:

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS 15.x
- Runtime/container: local source checkout + local CLI against live state
- Model/provider: `openai-codex/gpt-5.4` via `openai-codex:rai@rbutera.com`
- Integration/channel (if any): none required; reproduced through `openclaw agent --session-id ...`
- Relevant config (redacted): state rooted at `/Users/rai/.openclaw`, persisted session metadata contained `/home/rai/.openclaw/agents/shikamaru/sessions/<id>.jsonl`

### Steps

1. Seed or retain a `sessions.json` entry for `agent:shikamaru:main` whose `sessionFile` is `/home/rai/.openclaw/agents/shikamaru/sessions/<id>.jsonl`.
2. Run `openclaw agent --agent shikamaru --session-id <id> --message "smoke" --json` on macOS with state rooted at `/Users/rai/.openclaw`.
3. Observe the failure before this patch, then rerun after the patch.

### Expected

- OpenClaw remaps the stale same-agent path into the current state dir and writes to the current session file.

### Actual

- Before the patch, embedded execution attempted `mkdir '/home/rai/.openclaw/agents/shikamaru/sessions'` and failed.

## Evidence

Attach at least one:

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets

## Human Verification (required)

target.title: fix(media): suppress default audio prompt for non-English hints
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #98970.

OpenClaw currently resolves the built-in English audio prompt (`Transcribe the audio.`) even when audio transcription has an explicit non-English language hint. For OpenAI-compatible Whisper providers such as Groq, that prompt is a decoding bias hint, so short non-English clips can be translated into English despite `language=ru`.

This is an alternative/replacement for #99008. It keeps the same narrow prompt/language fix direction while preserving the existing missing-provider diagnostic path that #99008 currently regresses.

## Why This Change Was Made

The audio runner already resolves language from the request override, entry, capability config, and shared media config. The prompt resolver did not see that language, so an omitted user prompt always became the English default.

This change makes audio prompt resolution language-aware:

- Explicit prompts still win and are passed through unchanged.
- No language hint, English hints (`en`, `eng`, `english`, `en-*`, `en_*`), and non-audio capabilities keep existing behavior.
- Non-English audio hints with no explicit prompt now leave provider `prompt` unset.
- The OpenAI-compatible audio adapter omits unset optional prompt fields from the multipart request while still sending the explicit `language` hint.

The existing `formatMissingProviderHint` export and missing-provider error suffix are untouched.

## User Impact

Users who configure non-English audio transcription, such as `language=ru`, no longer get the default English prompt injected into provider requests. This lets Groq/OpenAI-compatible Whisper honor the language hint without the English prompt bias reported in #98970.

English transcription and explicit `tools.media.audio.prompt` configurations keep their previous behavior.

target.title: fix(cron): expose flat cron job fields and normalize malformed tool args
target.body:
Related: #3569 
Related: #64721

## What Problem This Solves

`src/agents/tools/cron-tool.ts` exposes a TypeBox schema to models in Openclaw where almost everything is `Type.Optional`. However the contract is enforced downstream in `normalize.ts` and `persisted-shape.ts` meaning fields that looked optional become required depending on which `kind` was chosen. The code says at ln 54–55:

> "Spell out job/patch properties for model-facing schema; runtime validation still happens in
> normalizeCronJob* to avoid nested union schemas."

In practice this means that openclaw gets no useful feedback from mistakes. Typical failures seen in testing: emitting the `job` argument as a truncated string instead of an object; supplying a top-level `mode` (valid only for the `wake` action); choosing a schedule kind without its required field (e.g. `kind: "cron"` with no `expr`, or omitting `payload.kind`); and passing `toolsAllow`/`fallbacks` as a scalar string instead of an array. Rejection gives generic error messages such as "jobId required" and "job required" with no field-level detail, so the openclaw doesn't have sufficient information to fix the problem. 

## Why This Change Was Made

I mostly use local Gemma 4 26b Q5 which became  completely unable to amend my cron jobs following upgrade to v6 Openclaw. However this is not simply a local LLM issue as Codex also had difficulties. Codex's greater reasoning power allowed for workrounds but with clearer schema these workarounds and iterative fixes wouldn't be needed.

I see that #3569 reported the same issues and the report was later closed through PR #10776. But #10776 did not address the TypeBox schema. @gerroon reported that fails still happen on their Qwen-30b-Instruct after the fix.

Also #64721 reports the same kind of problem: `payload.model`, `payload.timeoutSeconds`,
`payload.contextTokens`, and `maxSpendUsd` are accepted at runtime but the schema rejects
them as unexpected properties.

 Fix could be with a discriminated union, making the model reason about nested conditional types. However my concern is that lower-reasoning local LLMs will not manage this reasoning adequately.

Therefore instead the patch adds a flat top-level field set as an alternative to the nested `job` object:

| Field           | Type    | Notes                                          |
| --------------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `name`          | string  | job name                                       |
| `enabled`       | boolean |                                                |
| `sessionTarget` | string  | `main \| isolated \| current \| session:<id>`  |
| `at`            | string  | ISO-8601, one-shot                             |
| `everyMs`       | integer | recurring interval in ms                       |
| `expr`          | string  | cron expression                                |
| `tz`            | string  | IANA timezone for `expr`                       |
| `message`       | string  | agentTurn prompt — implies `agentTurn` payload |
| `anchorMs`      | integer | start anchor for `everyMs` schedules           |
| `model`         | string  | agentTurn model override                       |
| `fallbacks`     | string[]| agentTurn fallback models                      |
| `toolsAllow`    | string[]| agentTurn allowed tool ids                     |
| `thinking`      | string  | agentTurn thinking override                    |
| `timeoutSeconds`| number  | agentTurn timeout override                     |

The canonicalizer (`cron-tool-canonicalize.ts`) infers `schedule.kind` and `payload.kind` from whichever fields are present, so the model never has to deal with the nested union. Also
descriptions for `text` (implies `systemEvent`) and `mode` (wake only, not delivery mode)
have been tightened up.

The implementation now also normalises scalar toolsAllow / fallbacks into arrays and reconstructs job / patch from recoverable flat fields when the request is clearly a cron add/update call.  This deals with an issue found in testing where openclaw incorrectly tries toolsAllow as a scalar string, or emits a malformed non-object job / patch alongside flat fields.  

## User Impact

Upstream already recovers flat params at runtime: 
`recoverCronObjectFromFlatParams` in `cron-tool-canonicalize.ts` (with
`CRON_FLAT_PAYLOAD_KEYS` / `CRON_FLAT_SCHEDULE_KEYS`)

The patch simply exposes in the model-facing schema what the runtime already accepts but doesn't show. Note the nested `job` form still works also.  There is no negative user impact to the fix.

## Evidence

Tested on OpenClaw gateway version 2026.6.10
OS: Linux Mint 22.3 (Zena)
Kernel: Linux 6.17.0-23-generic (x86_64)
LLMs used for testing: Local Gemma 4 26b Q5 (llama.cpp); openai/gpt-5.4
Tests designed and run by: Claude (Anthropic Claude Opus 4.8); OpenAI Codex (gpt-5.4)

Focused validation on `fix/cron-tool-schema-fix` (`~/code/openclaw-main`) currently passes for the actual patch surface:

- `corepack pnpm test src/agents/tools/cron-tool.schema.test.ts src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts`
  - schema shard: `20 passed`
  - agents shard: `135 passed`

These tests cover:

- flat-field exposure in the model-facing cron schema
- canonicalization of malformed flat `toolsAllow` / `fallbacks`
- synthesis of `job` / `patch` from recoverable flat arguments
- the drift guard that ensures any advertised flat field is still recoverable by the canonicalizer

Earlier branch testing also included:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/cron-tool.schema.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/cron-tool.test.ts`
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test`

Live installed testing on patched OpenClaw 2026.6.10 also succeeded in creating disposable cron jobs through the flat-field interface, confirming the path works in a real installed gateway and not only in unit tests.

This four-file branch is green on the patch-local validation that actually exercises the cron-tool
change. The remaining PR-guide blockers are upstream baseline failures outside this patch scope.

Current upstream-baseline validation also shows:

- latest `origin/main` still fails `corepack pnpm deps:shrinkwrap:check` with
  `npm-shrinkwrap.json is stale. Run pnpm deps:shrinkwrap:generate.`
- clean `origin/main` is also currently red in unrelated test areas, including
  `src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts` and `src/media-understanding/image.test.ts`
  (reported for completeness only)

So the branch is green for the cron-tool patch itself, while the remaining `check` / full-suite
`test` reds are upstream, pre-existing, and unrelated to this four-file change. codex review --base origin/main stated the patch appears to correctly expose the flat cron fields and normalize them before validation without introducing a concrete regression in the touched surfaces.

target.title: # PR: Filesystem Access Control (PathGuard)
target.body:
# PR: Filesystem Access Control (PathGuard)

## Summary

This PR introduces a stricter, policy-driven filesystem access layer (**PathGuard**) for OpenClaw agent filesystem tools, including local media (image/pdf) loaders.

It closes key security and consistency gaps by:
- canonicalizing requested paths before evaluation (realpath-aware, ENOENT-safe),
- preventing traversal and symlink/junction escapes,
- enforcing `allowedPaths` / `denyPaths` consistently for classic filesystem tools **and** local media loads,
- preserving **deny-overrides-allow** semantics,
- anchoring workspace-relative policy entries to the workspace root (and re-anchoring after realpath),
- treating `allowedPaths: []` as an explicit **deny-all**,
- supporting absolute glob policy entries (via minimatch) alongside canonical absolute literals,
- returning structured, remediation-focused policy denial tool results (`policy_denied`) when access is blocked,
- and enforcing a monotonic filesystem policy ceiling for spawned subagents (global + agent + subagent defaults + spawn-time tightening), plumbed end-to-end into the spawned run.

**Important scope note:**

R: “This PR secures filesystem tools; it does not sandbox arbitrary shell execution.”

Remote URLs (`http(s)://`) and inline `data:` inputs are not treated as filesystem paths and are outside this layer.

---

## Change Type

- [x] Feature
- [x] Security hardening
- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Docs
- [x] Tests

---

## Linked Issues

- Closes #39672
- Related #8719

---

## Problem Statement (What was wrong before)

Before this PR, filesystem tool enforcement had multiple gaps:

1) **Path canonicalization and symlink escape handling were fragmented**
- Traversal protections and “what path are we actually touching?” logic were spread across tools/flows.
- Non-existent paths (ENOENT) were tricky: naive realpath calls fail and can allow later-creation escapes.

2) **Policy matching was inconsistent**
- Absolute vs relative entries could be evaluated in different “path spaces”.
- Glob vs non-glob entries could diverge in behavior, especially when “roots” filtering was used as an approximation.

3) **Media tools could diverge from file tool policy**
- Local file references inside image/pdf flows could reopen outside-workspace reads if not enforced per resolved file.

4) **Sandbox and host flows lacked a unified enforcement story**
- Enforcement needed to be identical regardless of whether the run is sandboxed or host-based.

5) **Spawned subagents did not have a guaranteed filesystem policy ceiling**
- Subagents needed an explicit, monotonic ceiling that could not be loosened at spawn time.

---

## What Changed (Design + Implementation)

### 1) Core PathGuard enforcement (`src/security/path-guard.ts`)

PathGuard implements:

- **Canonical resolution for existing paths** via `fs.realpath`.
- **Nearest-existing-parent resolution** for ENOENT paths (prevents “create later via symlink” bypass).
- **Symlink/junction-aware comparisons** in canonical path space.
- **Deny precedence**: deny rules always override allow rules.
- **Workspace-only boundary**: `workspaceOnly` blocks outside-workspace access.
- **Relative entry anchoring**: workspace-relative policy entries are anchored to the workspace root, and re-anchored after realpath resolution.
- **Empty allowlists**: `allowedPaths: []` is treated as an explicit deny-all.
- **Absolute policy entries**:
  - absolute **literals** are canonicalized before comparison,
  - absolute **globs** are supported (matched against canonical real paths) without attempting to realpath the pattern.
- **Glob detection** via `Minimatch(...).hasMagic()` (brace/extglob supported).

### 2) Filesystem tool integration (read/write/edit/apply_patch-style)

- Tool FS config is resolved through the tool/fs policy configuration and enforced using `checkPathGuardStrict(...)`.
- Wrappers normalize args and run PathGuard checks on resolved paths.
- `apply_patch` is explicitly guarded by parsing patch hunks and enforcing FS policy on each patch target path (not just args.path/file_path).

### 3) Structured `policy_denied` tool result (model guidance)

When PathGuard denies access, tools return a structured tool result (instead of only throwing a raw error) that:
- states the restriction is system-enforced and cannot be bypassed,
- describes what the tool attempted to do,
- provides actionable remediation options,
- and explicitly points to config keys that can be changed to grant access.

This improves model behavior: fewer useless retries, more direct user remediation.

### 4) Media tool integration (image/pdf local paths)

Local media loads are now policy-checked on the resolved file path:
- `src/agents/tools/image-tool.ts`
- `src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.ts`

Key invariant:
- enforcement is per resolved path using `checkPathGuardStrict(...)`, not via root-prefix approximations.

### 5) Sandbox behavior

For local media loads in sandbox mode:
- PathGuard runs in sandbox flows too,
- policy root uses `sandbox.root` when sandboxed,
- otherwise `workspaceDir` is used.

### 6) Subagent filesystem policy ceiling (spawn-time tightening + runtime enforcement)

Goal: spawned subagents must never receive broader filesystem access than the configured ceiling.

Policy sources (monotonic tightening):
- Global: `tools.fs`
- Per-agent: `agents.<id>.tools.fs`
- Subagent defaults/ceiling: `tools.subagents.fs`
- Sessions-spawn defaults/ceiling: `tools.sessions_spawn.fsPolicy` (applied when the tool call omits `sessions_spawn.fsPolicy`)
- Spawn-time tightening: `sessions_spawn.fsPolicy`

Merge semantics:
- `workspaceOnly`: OR
- `denyPaths`: UNION
- `allowedPaths`: enforced as a ceiling/tightening model (empty list = deny all)

Persistence + plumbing:
- Effective policy is persisted on the spawned child session (`spawnedToolFsPolicy`) via `sessions.patch`.
- Gateway plumbs it into the child run as ingress field `toolFsPolicy`.
- Gateway session resets (`/new` / `/reset`) preserve `spawnedToolFsPolicy` (no widening after reset).
- Embedded runner passes it into tool construction.
- `createOpenClawCodingTools` accepts an `fsPolicy` override and uses it as the effective policy for that run.
- Nested spawns inherit the parent session’s `spawnedToolFsPolicy` ceiling before applying config/tool-call tightening.

---

## Configuration (for contributors)

### Filesystem policy knobs

- `tools.fs.workspaceOnly: boolean`
- `tools.fs.allowedPaths: string[] | undefined` (empty array means deny-all)
- `tools.fs.denyPaths: string[] | undefined`

Subagent ceiling:
- `tools.subagents.fs.{workspaceOnly, allowedPaths, denyPaths}`

Sessions-spawn defaults + spawn-time tightening:
- `tools.sessions_spawn.fsPolicy` (config default ceiling/tightening)
- `sessions_spawn.fsPolicy` (tool arg tightening; can only further restrict)

Notes:
- Deny always wins.
- Relative entries are workspace-anchored.
- Policies are evaluated against canonicalized real paths.

---

## Explicit Non-Goals / Out of Scope

- Exec sandboxing is not implemented here.
  R: “This PR secures filesystem tools; it does not sandbox arbitrary shell execution.”
- No shell argument parsing.
- Remote source governance is out-of-scope.

---

## Implementation Notes (for contributors)

### Policy evaluation edge cases covered

- `allowedPaths: []` is treated as an explicit **deny-all** (not “no restriction”).
- Relative literal entries are **re-anchored after realpath**: if a workspace-relative entry canonicalizes outside the workspace (e.g. it points at a symlink to an external dir), it **does not** match outside-workspace targets.
- Absolute glob entries support symlink-alias authoring by **canonicalizing the non-glob prefix** before matching.
  - When rebuilding the rewritten pattern, the implementation **normalizes slash joining** so root-anchored globs stay semantically equivalent (e.g. `"/**/*.pem"` must not become `"//**/*.pem"`).

### Tool behavior on denial (model guidance)

When a filesystem access is blocked by PathGuard, tools return a structured `policy_denied` result (English text + structured fields) so models:
- do not attempt “bypass retries”,
- clearly communicate what was attempted,
- present actionable remediation options,
- and point to config keys (`tools.fs.*`) for operators to change if access is intended.

### Subagent filesystem ceiling (monotonic tightening)

Effective subagent policy is computed as a ceiling and is monotonic (cannot be widened by spawn calls):
- global: `tools.fs`
- agent: `agents.<id>.tools.fs`
- subagent defaults/ceiling: `tools.subagents.fs`
- sessions-spawn defaults: `tools.sessions_spawn.fsPolicy`
- spawn-time tightening: `sessions_spawn.fsPolicy` / tool arg `sessions_spawn.fsPolicy`

Merge intent:
- `workspaceOnly`: OR
- `denyPaths`: UNION
- `allowedPaths`: ceiling/tightening model (empty list = deny all)

The effective ceiling is persisted on the child session (`spawnedToolFsPolicy`) and forwarded into the embedded runner (`toolFsPolicy` → `createOpenClawCodingTools({ fsPolicy })`).

---

## Verification

- CI checks and tests pass (per latest runs).
- Added/maintained coverage ensuring `tools.sessions_spawn.fsPolicy` is applied as a default tightening when the tool call omits `sessions_spawn.fsPolicy`.
- Verified critical denial scenarios: traversal, symlink/junction escapes, ENOENT parent-walk, deny precedence, empty allowlist deny-all, sandbox media enforcement, apply_patch enforcement, and subagent ceiling propagation.
- Verified monotonic nested spawning: a tightened subagent cannot spawn a child with broader FS access (parent `spawnedToolFsPolicy` is inherited).
- Verified gateway resets (`/new` / `/reset`) preserve the spawned FS ceiling (no widening after reset).

---

## Reviewer / Contributor Notes (Do not regress these invariants)

- Do not replace per-path enforcement with root-prefix approximations for glob policies.
- Keep deny-overrides-allow.
- Keep relative policy entries anchored to workspace (including after realpath).
- Keep sandbox and host local-file enforcement aligned.
- Keep local filesystem policy and remote-source policy separate concepts.
- Keep subagent policy tightening monotonic (no privilege escalation vs ceiling).
- Remember: exec is outside this enforcement layer.

---

## Rollback / Recovery

- Disable restrictions by setting `workspaceOnly: false` and clearing `allowedPaths` / `denyPaths`.
- No data migration required.

target.body:
## Summary

- Replaces the 7 bare successful-response `res.json()` calls in `extensions/msteams/src/graph-upload.ts` with the shared bounded provider JSON reader.
- Covers OneDrive uploads, SharePoint uploads, sharing links, driveItem properties, chat list resolution, and chat member enumeration.
- Rebased onto latest `upstream/main`, where `readProviderJsonResponse` reads JSON through `readResponseWithLimit` with the shared 16 MiB cap.
- Adds real `node:http` loopback proof for normal chunked JSON, malformed JSON labelling, and oversized success JSON rejection.

## Linked context

No linked issue; this is a narrow follow-up to the bounded-response-read hardening series.

Related #97711 (same file family, but this PR includes loopback proof and complete PR context).

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** 7 unbounded successful Microsoft Graph API JSON reads in `graph-upload.ts` (`uploadToOneDrive`, `createSharingLink`, `uploadToSharePoint`, `getDriveItemProperties`, `resolveGraphChatId`, `getChatMembers`, `createSharePointSharingLink`).
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86-64, Node 22/24 compatible repo environment, latest `upstream/main` after rebase on 2026-06-29.

## Summary

- Problem: OpenClaw only derives failover candidates from `agents.defaults.model.fallbacks`, so operators who keep multiple models in `agents.defaults.models` still have to duplicate that ordered list manually.
- Why it matters: if the configured primary becomes unavailable, the runtime stops at the primary unless the same catalog is copied into `fallbacks`, which is easy to miss and easy to drift.
- What changed: added an explicit opt-in `agents.defaults.model.fallbacksFromModels: true` that derives fallback candidates from `agents.defaults.models` in config order when explicit `fallbacks` are omitted.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): this PR does not change existing fallback error classification, auth-profile rotation behavior, or the meaning of explicit `fallbacks` / `fallbacks: []`.

## Summary

Adds a bundled xAI realtime voice provider for OpenClaw Talk `gateway-relay`.

The provider connects to xAI realtime voice (`grok-voice-latest`) and maps the realtime WebSocket event stream into OpenClaw's existing Talk realtime provider contract. This gives OpenClaw users another native realtime voice supplier without turning the path into a local STT -> TTS loop.

## What changed

- Added `extensions/xai/realtime-voice-provider.ts`.
- Registered the realtime voice provider from the xAI plugin entrypoint and manifest.
- Moved `ws` to runtime dependencies for the xAI extension.
- Added unit coverage for xAI session setup, audio/text/transcript events, tool calls, error paths, close handling, and VAD bounds.
- Added Talk UI regression coverage for gateway-relay fallback from `talk.client.create` to `talk.session.create`.
- Documented xAI realtime voice setup in `docs/providers/xai.md`.

## Why

This may not be the highest priority for every OpenClaw deployment, but it is important for users building practical long-running voice assistants where supplier choice and cost matter. xAI realtime voice gives another native option for people who want realtime voice in OpenClaw without being locked into a single provider or falling back to a less natural STT -> TTS loop.

target.title: fix(cron): pass allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent from cron executor for both runner paths
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #94224: cron jobs that intentionally produce empty replies (silent alert watchers — "watch X, say nothing unless there is something to report") fail every run with `FailoverError: CLI backend returned an empty response` even when the underlying runner returns success.

Supersedes PR #94491 which used a lane substring heuristic in the shared CLI runner. Per ClawSweeper review, the correct boundary is the cron executor.

## What Problem This Solves

Cron jobs configured as silent alert watchers fail on every scheduled run with `empty_response` errors. The `allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent` flag exists in the runner infrastructure but the cron executor never sets it — it is only computed for DM/group chat contexts.

## Root cause

The `allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent` flag is only computed for DM/group chat contexts. The cron executor never sets it, so both the CLI and embedded runner paths throw `FailoverError("empty_response")` on empty output.

## Changes

In `src/cron/isolated-agent/run-executor.ts`: set `allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent: true` on both runner calls:

1. **CLI path** (`runCliAgent` call, line 326): added flag
2. **Embedded path** (`runEmbeddedAgent` call, line 429): added flag

This is a +6 line change to a single file. No changes to the shared `cli-runner.ts` guard.

## Evidence

### 1: Bug confirmed in production binary (OpenClaw v2026.6.10)

The current npm release does **not** set `allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent` in the cron executor:

```
$ grep -c "allowEmptyAssistantReplyAsSilent" \
  node_modules/openclaw/dist/server-cron-*.js
server-cron-Dcw720HP.js:0
server-cron-FMtfxqjb.js:0
```

The flag infrastructure exists in the generic agent runner but the cron executor never passes it.

### 2: Fix applied on both paths

target.title: fix(agents): handle explicit empty tool lists in system prompt
target.body:
## Summary

Describe the problem and fix in 2-5 bullets:

- Problem: when tools are explicitly disabled for a session, OpenClaw can still build a prompt that looks partly like a normal tool-enabled session. That can leave behind leaked skills content or other tool-only guidance.
- Why it matters: if the prompt says the session has tools when it actually does not, the model can try to use tools that are unavailable and behave like a tool-enabled session instead of a chat-only one.
- What changed: this PR makes the no-tools case consistent in the code that builds and adjusts the system prompt. The final prompt, prompt report, CLI path, embedded-runner path, and OpenAI-specific no-tools wording now all agree when a session really has no tools. It also fixes skills reporting in cases where the prompt contains another <available_skills> block or a skill body contains headings like # Project Context. Before this change, the prompt report could read the wrong block or stop too early, which could make it show missing or partial skills even though the real prompt still contained them.
- Additional behavior corrected: sessions that only have hosted/client tools no longer advertise OpenClaw built-in tool flows such as exec or subagents when those built-in tools are not actually available.
- Small contract update: provider-specific prompt code now receives `toolNames` in the `transformSystemPrompt` context, so plugins see the same advertised tool list that the main prompt builder is using.
- Scope boundary: this PR does not broadly redesign all capability handling. Sessions with omitted tool lists or non-empty filtered tool lists are still left mostly unchanged unless a narrow fix was needed to keep the no-tools and hosted-tool-only cases truthful.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes N/A
- Related #25569, #53000, #46214
- Adjacent context: #44229, #44484, #47583
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause / Regression History (if applicable)

- Root cause: when OpenClaw builds the system prompt for a session with no tools, different parts of the prompt-building flow can disagree about whether tools are available. Some parts correctly treat the session as tool-free, while others still act as if tools or skills exist, so the final prompt can end up mixing no-tool behavior with tool-related guidance.
- Missing detection / guardrail: there was no coverage that locked in this behavior across the full flow, including the prompt text, prompt report, CLI path, embedded-runner path, provider-specific prompt code, and OpenAI-specific no-tools wording.
- Prior context (`git blame`, prior PR, issue, or refactor if known): #25569 is still the closest related upstream work because it distinguishes explicitly empty tool availability from unspecified/default availability, but other code paths still had inconsistent behavior. #53000 addresses similar empty-tools confusion but still keeps a reference tool catalog in the prompt. #46214 removes adjacent CLI-runner prompt pollution rather than this exact bug.
- Why this reproduces: the no-tools state was not carried through every step that contributes to the final prompt. Once a real runtime session had tools intentionally disabled, some later steps still added skills content or other tool-related guidance.
- What was ruled out: this is not just a unit-test-only mismatch. The same problem was reproduced through the normal OpenClaw CLI against an isolated deployment config, and review also surfaced related inconsistencies in provider-specific prompt code and OpenAI no-tools wording.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [ ] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file:
  - `src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/system-prompt-report.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/system-prompt.memory.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/cli-runner.spawn.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/system-prompt.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/tool-name-allowlist.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/compaction-runtime-context.test.ts`
  - `extensions/openai/index.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in:
  - explicit empty-tool sessions must not leak the skills catalog
  - explicit empty-tool sessions must not leak later tool-only guidance such as tool-call style, subagent/tool messaging guidance, approvals, or sandbox guidance
  - explicit empty-tool sessions must preserve truthful non-tool context such as workspace notes and TTS hints
  - prompt reports for explicit empty-tool sessions must keep `tools.entries = []` and no skills block
  - omitted `toolNames` must preserve legacy/default prompt behavior
  - explicit non-empty filtered tool lists must stay close to upstream/main behavior
  - client-tool-only sessions must not advertise native OpenClaw exec/subagent flows
  - provider overlays and transform hooks must receive the same effective tool context as the final prompt
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the final bug surface spans prompt construction, prompt reporting, runner plumbing, and provider overlays, so the reliable guardrail has to cover those seams rather than only the original builder helper.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): none previously separated omitted tools from explicit empty effective tools across the whole prompt pipeline, and none previously locked in the client-tool-only/provider-transform cases.
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Sessions with tools explicitly disabled now behave like true no-tool sessions:

- no leaked skills catalog
- no later tool-only guidance such as tool-call style, approval flow, subagent orchestration, tool-only messaging, or sandbox execution hints
- prompt report for the explicit no-tools path no longer includes a skills block
- OpenAI no-tools wording now stays aligned with the no-tools path instead of reintroducing tool-related wording
- workspace notes and TTS hints can still appear when supplied because they are context, not tool availability

Additional fixes covered by this branch:

- sessions that only have hosted/client tools no longer advertise OpenClaw built-in exec/subagent flows they do not actually have
- CLI and bundled-tool sessions continue to advertise truthful tool guidance when tools really are available
- provider-specific prompt code now receives the tool-name context it needs to make consistent prompt adjustments

Sessions with omitted tool lists and explicit non-empty filtered tool lists are still left close to existing behavior unless a narrow consistency fix required otherwise.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[toolNames omitted or []] -> [shared prompt construction] -> [explicit no-tools sessions can still inherit skills content or tool-related guidance]

After:
[toolNames omitted] -> [legacy/default prompt behavior]
[toolNames non-empty] -> [upstream/main-style filtered prompt behavior]
[toolNames = []] -> [explicit no-tools branch] -> [truthful no-tool prompt with no leaked skills block or tool-only guidance]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: N/A

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux (Debian bookworm host)
- Runtime/container: local source checkout run via pnpm; not a containerized repro
- Model/provider: `openai-codex/gpt-5.4`
- Integration/channel (if any): CLI via `openclaw agent --local`
- Relevant config (redacted): temporary `no-tools` agent with `tools: { deny: ["*"] }`

### Steps

1. Create a disposable config copy and add a temporary no-tool agent so the runtime has a truly empty effective tool set:

   ```bash
   export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/path/to/openclaw.json
   export OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/path/to/state-dir

   cp "$OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH" /tmp/openclaw-no-tools-repro.json
   export OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/openclaw-no-tools-repro.json

   python3 - <<'PY'
   import json, os
   p = os.environ["OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH"]
   with open(p) as f:
       cfg = json.load(f)
   agents = cfg.setdefault("agents", {}).setdefault("list", [])
   agents = [a for a in agents if a.get("id") != "no-tools"]
   agents.append({
       "id": "no-tools",
       "tools": {"deny": ["*"]},
   })
   cfg["agents"]["list"] = agents
   with open(p, "w") as f:
       json.dump(cfg, f, indent=2)
       f.write("\n")
   PY
   ```

2. Run the normal CLI repro against that config:

   ```bash
   openclaw agent --local \
     --agent no-tools \
     --session-id explicit-empty-tools-repro \
     --json \
     --message '/context detail' \
     --timeout 120 \
   | jq '{payloads, tools: .meta.systemPromptReport.tools, skills: .meta.systemPromptReport.skills, systemPrompt: .meta.systemPromptReport.systemPrompt}'
   ```

### Expected

- In a real explicit no-tool session:
  - `tools.entries` should be `[]`
  - `tools.listChars` should be `0`
  - the prompt should not inject the skills catalog
  - the prompt should explicitly behave like a no-tools session

### Actual

- Live deployed-instance repro on this fixed branch:
  - `tools.entries = []`
  - `tools.listChars = 0`
  - `skills.promptChars = 0`
  - `skills.entries = []`
  - `systemPrompt.chars = 20194`
  - final assistant text includes `No tools are available in this session.`
- Live deployed-instance repro on v2026.04.11:
  - `tools.entries = []`
  - `tools.listChars = 0`
  - `skills.promptChars = 5932`
  - `skills.entries.length = 11`
  - `systemPrompt.chars = 30389`

## Evidence

Attach at least one:

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

Evidence highlights:
- Live repro on this branch:
  - `tools.entries = []`
  - `tools.listChars = 0`
  - `skills.promptChars = 0`
  - `skills.entries = []`
  - `systemPrompt.chars = 20194`
  - assistant text explicitly says `No tools are available in this session.`
- Live repro on `v2026.4.11`:
  - `tools.entries = []`
  - `tools.listChars = 0`
  - `skills.promptChars = 5932`
  - `skills.entries.length = 11`
  - `systemPrompt.chars = 30389`
- Targeted prompt/report tests on this branch:
  - `src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/system-prompt-report.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/system-prompt.memory.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/cli-runner.spawn.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/system-prompt.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/tool-name-allowlist.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/compaction-runtime-context.test.ts`
  - `extensions/openai/index.test.ts`
  - result: `150` tests passed across `8` files

## Human Verification (required)

What you personally verified (not just CI), and how:

- Verified scenarios:
  - reran the deployed-instance repro on an isolated OpenClaw instance using a disposable no-tools config
  - confirmed the bug still reproduces on `main` and `v2026.4.11`
  - confirmed the same repro no longer fails on this fixed branch
  - confirmed the verification signal is prompt/report metadata, not model-specific assistant output
- Edge cases checked:
  - explicit empty-tool session keeps `tools.entries = []` and `tools.listChars = 0`
  - explicit empty-tool session no longer leaks the skills catalog or later tool-only guidance
  - client-tool-only sessions no longer advertise native OpenClaw exec/subagent flows they do not actually have
- What you did **not** verify:
  - full OpenClaw test suite
  - unrelated model-level or workflow-level regressions outside this prompt-construction/reporting bug
  - performance impact beyond the prompt/report character-count change above

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

If a bot review conversation is addressed by this PR, resolve that conversation yourself. Do not leave bot review conversation cleanup for maintainers.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Config/env changes? (`Yes/No`) No
- Migration needed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If yes, exact upgrade steps: N/A

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: callers that accidentally relied on tool-related guidance surviving in explicit empty-tool sessions will now get a true no-tool prompt.
  - Mitigation: that behavior now matches explicit runtime intent, and regression tests lock in the distinction.
- Risk: future prompt edits could blur the difference between omitted, explicit empty, and explicit non-empty filtered tool states.
  - Mitigation: regression tests now cover all three cases.

target.title: fix: A2A handoffs can duplicate message-tool replies
target.body:
Related: #39476
Related: #91161
Related: #93293

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users asking an agent to hand work to another session could receive duplicate visible output when the target session replied through `message(action="send")` and the waited A2A path later treated transcript bookkeeping as a fresh assistant reply.

This PR was triggered by a real local WhatsApp/Main Merid duplicate-delivery report. The private message content is intentionally not included, but the observed shape was: one correct requester-visible reply, followed by a second visible message derived from the same A2A/source-reply flow.

This is a narrow companion to #39476. It does not replace #91161's reverse `sessions_send` tool guard, and it does not change compaction replay behavior covered by #93293.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix keeps waited A2A reply extraction on model-authored assistant replies instead of transcript artifacts. It excludes inter-session input rows, raw OpenClaw delivery mirrors, projected message-tool mirrors, and Gateway-injected assistant rows before they can feed ping-pong or announce delivery.

It also keeps same-session A2A source replies from re-running the announce decider when there is no valid announce target, and treats incomplete-turn fallback text as non-deliverable in the A2A announce path.

No production config, secrets, channel adapter contract, tool schema, delivery API, runtime permission, package metadata, or changelog file is changed.

## User Impact

A2A handoffs that reply visibly through the message tool no longer turn already-delivered source replies or forwarded `sessions_send` transcript rows into a second visible message. Normal model-authored assistant replies still use the existing waited reply, ping-pong, and announce behavior.

## Evidence

target.title: feat(doctor): add Node.js runtime info health contribution
target.body:
## Summary
Add a new Doctor health contribution that displays Node.js runtime
diagnostics during `openclaw doctor`, providing essential context for
troubleshooting and proactive upgrade guidance.
## What it does
**Runtime summary note** (always shown):
Node 24.14.0 · ~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.14.0/bin/node · via nvm
**Version manager detection** — identifies nvm, fnm, volta, asdf, n,
nodenv, nodebrew, and nvs from the executable path.
**Proactive warnings** (when applicable):
- Node version below minimum (>=22.19.0) — rarely triggers since the
  startup gate catches this first, but guards edge cases
- Node release in maintenance phase — shows months remaining until EOL
- Node release past end-of-life — recommends a current Active LTS release
- Older-than-recommended LTS — gentle nudge toward the recommended LTS
## Why
Doctor currently has no visibility into the Node.js runtime environment.
When users share Doctor output in issues or with maintainers, the Node
version and installation method are critical diagnostic context that was
previously missing.
This reuses existing infrastructure:
- `runtime-guard.ts` — `detectRuntime()`, `parseSemver()`, `runtimeSatisfies()`
- `runtime-paths.ts` — `isVersionManagedNodePath()`
No new dependencies. No runtime behavior changes outside of Doctor.
## Changes
New files:
- `src/commands/doctor-node-runtime.ts` (~200 lines) — diagnostics
  collection, warning generation, summary formatting, contribution entry
- `src/commands/doctor-node-runtime.test.ts` — 27 unit tests
Modified:
- `src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.ts` — +1 import, +1 wrapper
  function, +1 contribution registration (after `bundled-plugin-runtime-deps`,
  before `state-integrity`)
## Test plan
- `pnpm check` — 0 errors ✅
- `vitest` — 27/27 tests ✅
- `pnpm build` — clean ✅
Test coverage:
- `detectVersionManagerName`: 11 tests (null, system, nvm, fnm, volta,
  asdf, n, nodenv, nodebrew, nvs, Windows backslash)
- `collectNodeRuntimeDiagnostics`: 3 tests (nvm path, unknown runtime,
  system install)
- `buildNodeRuntimeWarnings`: 8 tests (recommended version, below
  minimum, past EOL, maintenance phase, pre-maintenance nudge, current
  recommended, null major, future major)
- `buildNodeRuntimeSummary`: 5 tests (system install, named manager,
  unknown manager, null version, separator format)
---
## Real behavior proof
_Refreshed for current head `f90eee0a` (after the Windows case-insensitive OS-home redaction commit)._

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** The Doctor Node runtime note renders the executable path via a two-pass redaction (`shortenHomePath` for the OpenClaw home, then an OS-home pass). The OS-home pass compared the Windows home prefix with exact casing, so a valid Windows path whose drive/username casing differed from `os.homedir()` (e.g. `os.homedir()` = `C:\Users\Alice`, `execPath` = `c:\users\alice\...`) fell through unredacted and leaked the OS username. POSIX comparison stays case-sensitive; the Windows backslash-boundary prefix is now compared case-insensitively, slicing by the original length to preserve real casing.

- **Real environment tested:** Linux (Ubuntu 24.04, WSL2), Node.js 24.14.0, current PR head `f90eee0a`. Invoked the real `collectNodeRuntimeDiagnostics()` + `buildNodeRuntimeSummary()` — the same render `noteNodeRuntime()` emits in the Doctor health flow — plus injected lifecycle scenarios via the exported helpers.

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** ran the registered render path via tsx against the real runtime:
```bash
$ node --import tsx run-node-runtime-note.ts
```

- **Evidence after fix (current head):** Block 1 is the real render on this machine. Block 2 is the POSIX OS-home redaction scenario (OPENCLAW_HOME elsewhere). Block 3 is the new Windows case-insensitive redaction this commit fixes. Remaining blocks are injected lifecycle scenarios against the current date.
```
=== 1. Real current-head render (Node v24.14.0) ===
Node 24.14.0 · /usr/bin/node · system install

=== 2. POSIX OS-home redaction (OPENCLAW_HOME=/srv/openclaw, Node under the user's OS home) ===
os home (HOME)     : /home/<user>
input  execPath    : /home/<user>/.nvm/versions/node/v24.14.0/bin/node
output rendered    : Node 24.14.0 · ~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.14.0/bin/node · via nvm
leaks OS username? : NO (redacted)

=== 3. Windows case-insensitive redaction (the new fix) ===
os.homedir()       : C:\Users\Alice   (canonical casing)
input  execPath    : c:\users\alice\AppData\Roaming\nvm\v24.14.0\node.exe   (lower-cased)
output rendered    : Node 24.14.0 · ~\AppData\Roaming\nvm\v24.14.0\node.exe · via nvm
leaks OS username? : NO (redacted)

=== Injected Node 22 LTS (22.19.0, in maintenance) ===
Node 22 LTS is in maintenance mode (EOL 2027-04-30, ~10 months remaining).
Consider upgrading to Node 24 for the latest features and longer support.

=== Injected Node 20 (20.18.0, below the >=22.19.0 minimum) ===
Node 20.18.0 does not meet the minimum requirement (>=22.19.0).
Upgrade Node: https://nodejs.org/en/download
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The real Node 24.14.0 runtime renders a clean note (supported, system install). Both the POSIX OS-home scenario (block 2) and the Windows case-mismatch scenario (block 3) now redact the home to `~`, so no OS username appears — including when `execPath` casing differs from `os.homedir()`. Before this commit, the exact-case Windows prefix check left such paths unredacted. Injected Node 22 LTS / 20 produce the expected maintenance / below-minimum advisories. POSIX, Windows OPENCLAW_HOME-override, and the new Windows case-mismatch regression tests cover the redaction paths; 51 unit tests pass, types and lint clean.

- **What was not tested:** The full interactive `openclaw doctor` TUI run was not captured (it triggers a heavy dist build); the registered render path is invoked directly instead. Redaction relies on `os.homedir()`; in the rare case where `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` is unset and differs from the path's owner (e.g. some sudo/container setups), redaction may not apply — out of scope for this detect-only diagnostic.

target.title: fix(memory-host): add AbortSignal support to batch polling (OpenAI, Voyage, Gemini)
target.body:
Add AbortSignal support to batch polling loops to enable immediate cancellation when clients disconnect.

Problem
When HTTP clients disconnect during batch embedding operations, server-side polling continues until timeout, wasting API quota.

Solution
- Replace uncancelable setTimeout with cancellable version using clearTimeout
- Add signal?: AbortSignal parameter to all batch providers
- Use { once: true } to prevent listener accumulation (fixes MaxListenersExceededWarning)
- Thread signal through full call chain: batch-runner → runXxxBatches → waitForXxxBatch

Changes
- batch-runner.ts: Add signal to EmbeddingBatchExecutionParams type
- batch-openai.ts: Add signal support with {once: true} cleanup
- batch-voyage.ts: Update sleep type, add signal threading through deps
- batch-gemini.ts: Add signal support with {once: true} cleanup

Testing
- Verified polling stops within 1s of abort (was 30+ iterations)
- No listener leaks after long polls
- TypeScript compiles without errors

Backwards Compatible: signal is optional.

**Additional Fixes (Post-Review)**:
- Fixed `initial: batchInfo` parameter regression in `batch-voyage.ts` and `batch-gemini.ts` to avoid extra API calls on batch creation
- Fixed locale regression in `ui/src/ui/presenter.ts` (reverted hardcoded "en-US" to `undefined` for i18n compliance)

target.title: feat(durable): wire agent session runtime coordination
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

This PR wires the durable runtime foundation from PR2 into agent/session/subagent paths so OpenClaw can record durable context for chat sends, agent runs, subagent child runs, parent fan-in, yield progress, and restart/recovery inspection.

The target behavior is: parent agents should have durable child/fan-in state; one failed child should not make sibling completion invisible; and Gateway/session restart should leave inspectable runtime state instead of silent coordinator ambiguity.

## Dependency Chain

This is PR3 in the replacement durable runtime stack:

1. PR1: durable session/task runtime RFC v2.
2. PR2: durable runtime foundation.
3. PR3: agent/session/subagent wiring, this PR.

This branch is stacked on the refreshed PR2 branch. The upstream PR diff against `main` is cumulative. For delta-only review after PR2, use:

https://github.com/mjnkao/openclaw/compare/codex/openclaw-durable-runtime-foundation-v2-ready...codex/openclaw-durable-runtime-agent-v2-ready

## Summary

Adds:

- Gateway `chat.send` and `agent.run` durable context refs;
- user-turn transcript durable context propagation;
- embedded-agent yield progress for resumable parent turns;
- subagent child-run mirroring and parent fan-in association;
- task completion contract metadata for durable parent/child lifecycle;
- status-notice display metadata for durable/yield progress;
- protocol schema fields for durable context references.

## Explicit Non-Scope

- Work module.
- Workboard UI/tools.
- Task Flow projection adapters.
- Retention/compaction.
- Postgres/multi-worker lease contention.
- Durable write controls such as cancel/retry/resume/signal.

## Latest Reviewer Follow-Up

Updated on 2026-07-02 after the latest ClawSweeper P1/P2 findings.

Head: `df88764a9f`.

Addressed ClawSweeper findings:

- P1: confirmed backend ACP manual-spawn child turns no longer create duplicate Gateway CLI task rows when ACP metadata proves the ACP spawn control plane already owns the requester-visible task.

target.title: fix(process): resolve gemini .cmd shim on Windows in supervisor child adapter
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

- On Windows, using the `google-gemini-cli` provider fails with `spawn gemini ENOENT` because Node's `child_process.spawn` does not automatically resolve `.cmd` extensions (only `.exe`/`.com`)
- npm global installs on Windows create `.cmd` shim files, so `gemini` (and `claude`) need the `.cmd` suffix to be found by `spawn`
- Fixes #98573

## Why This Change Was Made

The supervisor child adapter (`src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.ts`) has a `resolveCommand` function that uses `resolveWindowsCommandShim` with a hardcoded allowlist of commands that should get `.cmd` appended on Windows. The list included `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, and `npx` but not `gemini` or `claude` — so spawning those CLI tools failed on Windows.

## User Impact

- Windows users can now use the `google-gemini-cli` and `claude-cli` providers without encountering `ENOENT` spawn errors
- No change on macOS or Linux (platform guard already skips non-Windows)

## Evidence

### Behavior or issue addressed
- On Windows, `spawn("gemini")` fails with ENOENT because Node only auto-resolves `.exe`/`.com` extensions, not `.cmd`
- The `resolveCommand` helper was missing `gemini` from its shim allowlist

### Real environment tested
- Local development environment (Linux, Node 22)
- Unit tests simulate Windows platform via `setPlatform("win32")` to verify cmd.exe wrapping behavior

### Exact steps or command run after this patch
```bash
pnpm test src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.test.ts
```

### Evidence after fix
```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  21 passed (21)
```

New regression tests added:
- `wraps gemini CLI command through trusted cmd.exe on Windows (#98573)` — verifies `gemini` → `gemini.cmd` wrapped via `cmd.exe` on Windows
- `wraps claude CLI command through trusted cmd.exe on Windows` — verifies `claude` → `claude.cmd` wrapped via `cmd.exe` on Windows
- `keeps gemini command unchanged on non-Windows platforms (#98573)` — verifies no `.cmd` suffix on Linux/macOS

Existing test `wraps Windows command shims through trusted cmd.exe` (for `pnpm`) already validates the same code path — the new entries follow the identical pattern.

### Observed result after fix
- On simulated Windows: `spawnArgs.argv` = `[cmd.exe, /d, /s, /c, "gemini.cmd --version"]` (shim resolved)
- On Linux: `spawnArgs.argv` includes `gemini` verbatim (no `.cmd` suffix)

### What was not tested
- Not tested on a real Windows machine (no Windows environment available). The unit tests use `setPlatform("win32")` to simulate the Windows code path and verify the exact spawn arguments.

## Tests and validation

```bash
pnpm test src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.test.ts  # 21 tests pass (was 18, +3 new)
```

## Risk checklist

- [x] No: Does this change affect user-visible behavior? (Only affects Windows CLI tool spawning, restoring expected behavior)
- [x] No: Does this change affect configuration surface?
- [x] No: Does this change affect security? (No change to security model; same pattern used for other CLI tools like pnpm/npm/yarn)
- [x] No: Does this change affect plugin APIs?
- [x] No: Does this change require documentation updates?

## Additional notes

AI-assisted fix. Similar to how `npm`, `pnpm`, `yarn`, and `npx` were already handled, `gemini` and `claude` now also get the `.cmd` shim resolution on Windows. The `resolveWindowsCommandShim` function in `src/process/windows-command.ts` already handles the platform check and extension detection — the only missing piece was the allowlist entry.

The sibling PR #98609 targets the same issue with a similar approach. Compared to that PR, this one also covers `claude` (which has the same Windows spawn issue) and includes tests for the non-Windows path.

target.title: fix(anthropic): accept Claude CLI apiKeyHelper auth
target.body:
Fixes #97489

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Anthropic turns routed through the Claude CLI backend could fail OpenClaw's pre-spawn auth gate with `missing-provider-auth` when Claude Code was authenticated by `~/.claude/settings.json` `apiKeyHelper` instead of macOS Keychain or `~/.claude/.credentials.json`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Claude Code treats a configured `apiKeyHelper` as a supported credential source for dynamic/proxy auth. OpenClaw now recognizes a non-empty helper setting as Claude CLI-managed auth evidence without executing the helper or persisting helper output.

The follow-up commit also addresses the review finding that helper auth must win over stale stored Claude OAuth/token credentials. `readClaudeCliCredentials` now checks helper presence before macOS Keychain or `.credentials.json`, so OpenClaw's auth status and synthetic auth path match Claude Code credential precedence.

## User Impact

Users with proxy, vault, or rotating-key Claude CLI setups can start OpenClaw turns through `agentRuntime.id: "claude-cli"` without creating a dummy `.credentials.json` file just to satisfy OpenClaw's auth check. Status and doctor surfaces identify helper-backed auth without presenting it as OAuth-only state.

## Evidence

- Source contract checked: Claude Code docs list `apiKeyHelper` as a custom credential script and include it before `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` and subscription OAuth credentials in authentication precedence: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/iam#credential-management
- Added mixed credential regression: `src/agents/cli-credentials.test.ts` covers `apiKeyHelper` plus stale `.credentials.json` plus an available Keychain mock and asserts helper wins without executing Keychain lookup.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts src/agents/cli-credentials.test.ts` -> `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 18 passed (18)`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts src/agents/auth-profiles.external-cli-sync.test.ts` -> `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 22 passed (22)`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-providers.config.ts extensions/anthropic/index.test.ts` -> `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 33 passed (33)`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts src/agents/model-auth.profiles.test.ts -t "accepts Claude CLI apiKeyHelper auth without a stored credential profile"` -> `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 1 passed | 70 skipped (71)`.
- `git diff --check`.

Local proof limits:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts src/agents/cli-credentials.test.ts src/agents/model-auth.profiles.test.ts src/agents/model-auth-label.test.ts src/agents/auth-profiles.external-cli-sync.test.ts src/agents/cli-auth-epoch.test.ts src/agents/model-auth-markers.test.ts` completed with 146/150 passing; the remaining 4 failures were Windows `EBUSY: resource busy or locked, unlink ... openclaw.sqlite[-wal|-shm]` cleanup errors in `src/agents/model-auth.profiles.test.ts`, not assertion failures in the changed credential precedence path.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts src/commands/doctor-claude-cli.test.ts` completed with 6/7 passing; the remaining failure is the existing Windows POSIX-path expectation in `resolveClaudeCliProjectDirForWorkspace`.
- Testbox-through-Crabbox was attempted with `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs run --provider blacksmith-testbox ...`, but this local environment's `crabbox` binary failed wrapper sanity checks before creating a Testbox lease, so no remote id was available.
Additional real setup proof after ClawSweeper review (2026-06-30):

- Isolated setup command used a temporary `HOME`, `USERPROFILE`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`; wrote only `~/.claude/settings.json` with `apiKeyHelper`; confirmed `~/.claude/.credentials.json` was absent and Anthropic auth env vars were cleared.
- `node --import tsx --input-type=module` invoked the real shared Claude CLI credential reader plus the Anthropic provider discovery synthetic-auth seam.
- Output: `CLAUDE_HELPER_REAL_SETUP_PROOF {"head":"326b76c24944994e24a4d453bfd85dd7420835f8","settingsJson":true,"credentialsJson":false,"envAnthropicApiKey":false,"sharedCredential":{"type":"api_key_helper","provider":"anthropic"},"syntheticAuth":{"apiKey":"openclaw:claude-cli-api-key-helper","source":"Claude CLI apiKeyHelper","mode":"api-key"},"missingProviderAuthAvoided":true}`.

target.title: fix(status): surface fallback model selections in status mismatch detection
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #96126: `openclaw status` and `session_status` collapse the active (fallback) model into the same `Model:` line as the configured primary, making it impossible to see at a glance whether a session is running its intended model or a fallback.

## What Problem This Solves

Operators running multi-model setups with fallback chains cannot tell whether a session is on its configured primary model or an automatic fallback. A session silently running on a fallback model shows no indication in `openclaw status` output.

## Changes (v2 — ClawSweeper rank-up)

4 files, +56/-11:

- **`status.summary.ts`**: Changed mismatch detection from `hasUserPinnedModelSelection()` to `entry?.modelOverride != null` so auto-fallback selections are also flagged
- **`status.command-sections.ts`**: Removed `modelSelectionReason` filter + fallback-specific wording
- **`status.summary.test.ts`** + **`status.command-sections.test.ts`**: Added coverage

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: Auto-fallback model selections hidden from `openclaw status` mismatch detection.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux Node 24, live Gateway (1.8.0), full repository checkout
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```shell
  # Live Gateway status check — command executes against real Gateway:
  $ openclaw status
  ```
  ```shell
  # Unit tests verify mismatch detection logic:
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/status.command-sections.test.ts --run
  $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/status.summary.test.ts --run
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: Terminal output:

target.title: fix(process): resolve Gemini CLI Windows shim
target.body:
## Summary

Fix Windows Gemini CLI launches by resolving the npm-installed `gemini` shim to `gemini.cmd` before the supervisor spawns child processes.

## Issue/Motivation

Fixes #98573.

On Windows, npm global binaries such as Gemini CLI are exposed through `.cmd` shims. The child supervisor already resolves npm/pnpm/yarn/npx through the trusted `cmd.exe` wrapper, but `google-gemini-cli` ultimately spawns bare `gemini`, which can fail with `spawn gemini ENOENT` even when `gemini --help` works in a terminal.

## Changes

- Add `gemini` to the Windows command shim allowlist used by the child process adapter.
- Add regression coverage for the low-level shim resolver.
- Add child-adapter coverage proving Windows `gemini --help` is invoked through trusted `cmd.exe /d /s /c gemini.cmd --help`.

## Testing

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.ts src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.test.ts src/process/windows-command.test.ts`
- `pnpm exec vitest run src/process/windows-command.test.ts src/process/supervisor/adapters/child.test.ts` — 2 files passed, 24 tests passed
- `git diff --check`
- Diff secret scan over added lines — no matches

Note: `pnpm lint:core` and a direct `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs ...` attempt were stopped locally because type-aware oxlint/tsgolint hung for several minutes on unrelated broad shards/files in this low-disk watchdog environment. The focused formatter and regression tests above passed.

## What Problem This Solves

Windows users who install Gemini CLI through npm can have `gemini` available in their terminal while Node child-process spawning still fails with `spawn gemini ENOENT`, because the runnable target is the npm `.cmd` shim. This prevents OpenClaw's `google-gemini-cli` backend from starting on Windows.

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix: strengthen macOS SQLite WAL checkpoint durability
target.body:
Closes #99066

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where macOS users could run OpenClaw SQLite WAL checkpoints without SQLite's macOS fullfsync checkpoint barrier enabled. The normal app behavior would not show an error, but recently checkpointed local state could be less durable than intended across abrupt power loss or OS crashes.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change enables `PRAGMA checkpoint_fullfsync = 1;` after WAL mode is turned on, only on macOS. The PRAGMA is treated as a best-effort durability upgrade: if a SQLite build rejects it, WAL setup continues with the existing autocheckpoint and rollback-on-unsupported-filesystem behavior.

## User Impact

Mac users get stronger SQLite WAL checkpoint durability without changing configuration. Linux and Windows behavior is unchanged, and older SQLite builds that do not support the PRAGMA continue to open and configure their stores normally.

## Evidence

Live macOS runtime proof from a real Node SQLite process on macOS 13.7.8, running this PR branch (`aa10f1dd2f58723d5c9769de52086115c1a308b9`):

```text
platform=darwin
macos=13.7.8
node=v22.22.0
branch=proof/sqlite-macos-checkpoint-fullfsync
head=aa10f1dd2f58723d5c9769de52086115c1a308b9
journal_mode=wal
checkpoint_fullfsync=1
wal_autocheckpoint=1000
maintenance_checkpoint=true
maintenance_close=true
(node:76412) ExperimentalWarning: SQLite is an experimental feature and might change at any time
```

The live probe created a temporary SQLite database, called `configureSqliteConnectionPragmas(db, { databasePath, checkpointIntervalMs: 0 })`, then queried:

```text
PRAGMA journal_mode;
PRAGMA checkpoint_fullfsync;
PRAGMA wal_autocheckpoint;
```

The observed `checkpoint_fullfsync=1` confirms the macOS PRAGMA is applied in a real SQLite process after WAL setup.

Additional validation:

- Source-level before condition: `configureSqliteWalMaintenance` enabled `journal_mode = WAL` and `wal_autocheckpoint`, but had no macOS branch for `checkpoint_fullfsync`.
- Added focused coverage that mocks `process.platform` to `darwin` and verifies WAL setup calls `PRAGMA checkpoint_fullfsync = 1;` immediately after enabling WAL mode.
- Added fallback coverage that makes the macOS `checkpoint_fullfsync` PRAGMA throw and verifies WAL setup continues to `wal_autocheckpoint`.
- Existing rollback/NFS/network-filesystem behavior remains pinned by the same `sqlite-wal.test.ts` suite with explicit non-macOS platform mocks where needed.
